item.title: Panic in Dallas: Cowboys defense holds emergency summit as season spirals after Bucs loss
item.description: DeMarvion Overshown reveals details of the Dallas Cowboys' defensive players-only meeting after surrendering 241 rushing yards to Tampa Bay.
item.content:encoded:
Five weeks into the season and fresh off an embarrassing loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the Dallas Cowboys are already breaking out the oldest crisis gimmick in football: the defensive players-only meeting.

Sitting at 2-3 and watching their defense get pushed around on a weekly basis, the entire unit gathered behind closed doors on Monday morning to air out their issues.

Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown described the session as a blunt "heart-to-heart."

"Looking ourselves in the mirror," Overshown said.

"Putting what we wanted our standard to be, we put that on the board. We went by bullet point, bullet point. Are we holding up to this? Are we being this? As a unit, how can we get closer? What is it? Just hearing from all of us. It really wasn't like a fire drill conversation, it was more so, 'What can I do to help you? What do I expect from you on Sundays, or every Monday walk throughs?' We've got to talk to each other like that because the ship is only going to go as far as the weakest person on the boat. As long as we all in this together, I think we're going to be great. I know we're going to be there."

JERRY JONES SLAMS TABLE AFTER DAK PRESCOTT THROWS CRITICAL LATE INTERCEPTION IN BRUTAL COWBOYS LOSS

Writing bullet points on a dry-erase board is cute, but it does not erase what happened against Tampa Bay.

Dallas got thoroughly embarrassed at home by a winless Buccaneers squad, surrendering 241 rushing yards and making an 0-4 offense look explosive.

The Cowboys surrendered 419 total yards, blew basic run fits, and failed to force a single takeaway. Through five weeks, Dallas has surrendered at least 375 yards every game. Management is now scrambling to stop the bleeding before a tough road trip to Green Bay.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Defensive coordinator Christian Parker is moving upstairs to the coaching booth, and longtime NFL coach Mike Pettine was hired as a senior assistant to provide adult supervision.

Meanwhile, Dallas hopes Overshown's return from a four-game hamstring injury adds badly needed speed.

Whiteboard therapy is fine, but unless this group starts tackling someone, the Cowboys' season is officially cooked.

item.title: Man who lived as woman for eight years warns surprising teen sexuality data may not tell full story
item.description: Walt Heyer says social media and peer pressure may explain why fewer teenagers now identify as gay or bisexual, casting doubt on CDC data trends.
item.content:encoded:
A man who spent eight years identifying as a woman is casting doubt on reports of a dramatic decline in teenagers identifying as gay or bisexual, warning that social media and peer pressure may be influencing how young Americans describe their sexual orientation.

Walt Heyer, who detransitioned roughly 40 years ago and now serves as a senior fellow at the Family Research Council, told Fox News Digital in an exclusive video interview he remains skeptical of the apparent shift, suggesting some teenagers may be reluctant to openly identify as gay or bisexual because of social pressures.

"I don't really believe that there's a big dramatic free fall," Heyer said, referring to recent reports about declining rates of gay and bisexual identification among some teenagers.

LOG CABIN REPUBLICANS REMOVES 'T' FROM LGBT ADVOCACY, SAYS 'RADICAL' TRANS ACTIVISTS ARE ERODING GAY SUPPORT

"I think what's happening is that, because of social media, there's a lot more influence on people who may not want to fall into that classification on a social media level and will withhold the fact that they are gay or bisexual but really don't want to openly admit it," Heyer said.

The comments come after The Washington Post highlighted CDC data showing that the percentage of ninth grade girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual fell from 30% in 2021 to 17% in 2025. The share identifying as bisexual alone dropped from 26% to 13% over the same period.

PRISHA MOSELY: AS A DETRANSITIONER AND MOM, I KNOW WHAT GENDER IDEOLOGY STOLE FROM ME

The percentage of boys identifying as gay or bisexual has remained largely unchanged over the past decade, while the share of high school girls identifying as lesbian or bisexual surged after the COVID-19 pandemic before beginning to decline, the Post reported.

Heyer, an author and co-author of multiple books, including "Trans Life Survivors" and "Paper Genders," and has spent years working with people questioning their gender identities, argued that social dynamics among young people could complicate attempts to interpret the findings.

"I've had actual people in school saying that they're bullied into identifying one way, or they're bullying and bullied to not identify that way," he said.

BLUE STATE SCHOOL DISTRICT ACCUSED OF DEFYING SUPREME COURT, HIDING GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS

Heyer also said he believes peer and societal pressures are significant factors in kids choosing to identify with something else that is not their biological sex.

"What's interesting about that is that many kids are sort of coerced by their peers to say things one way or the other, so I've been very skeptical about what the kids are saying, whether they're gay or bisexual," Heyer said. 

"I don't really believe that there's a big dramatic free fall. That was, I think, quoted as a free fall in the people identifying as gay or bisexual," he added. "I think what's happening is that, because of social media, there's a lot more influence on people who may not want to fall into that classification on a social media level and will withhold the fact that they are gay or bisexual but really don't want to openly admit it."

A DETRANSITIONER CONFRONTED A CALIFORNIA LAWMAKER ON THE HARMS OF GENDER TRANSITION. HERE'S WHY HE SPOKE OUT

Simply but perhaps most importantly, Heyer said he thinks adults should do a better job of only affirming what is true.

"I think that what I've really discovered is that we know now and have evidence, factual evidence, that nobody has ever changed their gender," Heyer said. "I went through the hormones, had all the surgeries, identified that way. So far in all world history, nobody has actually biologically changed their gender. This is a cosmetic social appearance. It is not a biological change.

"And when you come to that conclusion, you realize that really the procedures and these terminologies and labels, what I refer to as God rejecting labels, God rejecting procedures in every aspect. This is the way young people and adults reject God and say God doesn't exist by taking these labels on," he added. 

DETRANSITIONERS REVEAL HOW DOCTORS PUSHED THEM TOWARD LIFE-ALTERING TREATMENT AS TEENS

Heyer also urged researchers to conduct additional studies before concluding that the numbers reflect a lasting shift in sexual identity.

"I just think it's important for us to be much more thorough and go to other areas before we come to some conclusion that there's a giant, giant drop in these identities," he said. "I don't think we're there yet."

item.title: Former Chicago police detective linked by DNA to 8-year-old girl's cold-case murder, police say
item.description: DNA evidence and a fingerprint linked Thomas F. McInerney Jr., a former Chicago police detective, to the 1960 cold case murder of Gloria Kowalewicz.
item.content:encoded:
A former Chicago homicide detective has been identified as the killer of an 8-year-old girl who disappeared while walking to church in 1960, with authorities now examining other cases that may have involved the officer.

Thomas F. McInerney Jr. joined the Chicago Police Department in 1959, just one year before Gloria Kowalewicz was abducted and murdered. He later became a detective investigating violent crimes and remained with the department until retiring in 1987.

More than 65 years after the killing, Chicago police confirmed to Fox News Digital that advances in DNA technology and a preserved fingerprint helped investigators identify McInerney, who died in 2006 at age 70.

COLD CASE BREAKTHROUGH SOLVES TEEN KILLING AFTER SUSPECT LIVED FREE FOR DECADES: 'BETTER BE AFRAID'

Gloria disappeared Nov. 12, 1960, after leaving her home shortly before 8 a.m. to attend morning Mass at St. Mary of Mt. Carmel Church, just a few blocks away. Her body was discovered roughly four hours later in a ditch at a forest preserve southwest of Chicago. She had been shot and killed.

The murder prompted an extensive investigation, with police interviewing more than 1,300 people and knocking on hundreds of doors. Despite those efforts, the case remained unsolved for decades.

Investigators preserved evidence from the crime scene and surrounding area, including a bullet, Gloria's coat and shoes, and a white communion purse containing her prayer book. A fingerprint was also recovered from the purse's strap.

DISCARDED TRASH UNCAPS 41-YEAR-OLD MURDER CASE IN RITZY SEASIDE RESORT TOWN, AUTHORITIES SAY

Working with the FBI and Illinois State Police, investigators used modern forensic technology to link DNA and the preserved fingerprint to McInerney, according to the department.

"McInerney should never have worn the CPD star, and it is devastating to accept that he was never identified and held accountable while he was alive," Chicago police said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital.

The Cook County State's Attorney's Office is working to identify other cases that may have involved McInerney, according to The Associated Press.

KILLER EX-COP EXECUTED FOR CHILD'S SLAYING AS SHERIFF SAYS HE’S SURE SAME MONSTER MURDERED ANOTHER GIRL

Police said Gloria's parents died before learning who killed their daughter, but expressed hope that identifying McInerney would bring some closure to those who knew her.

McInerney later worked for the Federal Public Defender's Office in Nevada before retiring in 2004, according to the AP. He died two years later without facing charges in Gloria's murder.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Joe Manganiello's secret seven-year health battle that nearly killed him
item.description: Joe Manganiello reveals Sofia Vergara made the life-saving call to remove his large intestine while he was unconscious during a secret health crisis.
item.content:encoded:
Joe Manganiello is opening up about the secret health battle that nearly "took his life" over seven years.

Manganiello sat down with "CBS Mornings" to discuss his health and his newly released memoir, "Bloodlines." 

During his appearance, the actor told Gayle King he was offered the role as the main villain, Deathstroke, in Ben Affleck's canceled "Batman" movie.

He wrote in his memoir that, at the same time as the job offer, he was "dying." Manganiello received the call to appear in the movie in 2016.

"I got the call about a month out of the hospital after I collapsed on another set," Manganiello told King. "After about a year of feeling these mystery symptoms, I went into the hospital for two months straight and, at the end of my stay, they wound up having to remove my entire large intestine to save my life.

JOE MANGANIELLO DENIES SOFIA VERGARA’S CLAIM MARRIAGE ENDED BECAUSE HE WANTED A BABY: ‘SIMPLY NOT TRUE’

"They had split me open. My entire large intestine had turned to pus, and it was about to explode," he continued. "They took it out, and the surgery left me with an ostomy bag. And in the wake of that, I lost 60 pounds in two weeks. I couldn't walk. My eye went cross-eyed. I lost my voice. I had five catheters."

Manganiello explained that, after he was released from the hospital, he was in the process of trying to gain the weight back when he got the call to meet Affleck and appear in the "Batman" movie.

The actor told King he was still married to Sofia Vergara at the time, and she was the one who ultimately made the decision for the doctors to save his life and remove his large intestine.

"They had to call her as my next of kin and give her options of what she thought I would want done to me while I was unconscious. She chose the right one, and it bought me time," Manganiello said. "It didn't solve the problem. The doctors still had no idea what was causing this, how to treat it. But it bought me enough time."

"But we do have to credit her for saving your life. For making that decision," King replied.

"Absolutely," Manganiello said.

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

King went on to cite Manganiello's memoir in which he wrote that his mystery illness put a strain on his marriage to Vergara. The former couple married in 2015 and announced their separation in 2023. Their divorce was finalized in 2024.

"That kind of pain was like a flood in my life. You can't predict how that's going to affect people. It affected me a certain way, it affected her," he said. "It was seven years long. People didn't know about it. I was living in secret with this. Only the closest people around me knew."

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

King mentioned that Vergara's son, Manolo Gonzalez Vergara, 35, shared a post about a "narcissistic" man on Monday.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Her son posted a thing about, ‘This is what happens when you deal with a narcissistic man,’ and she has liked that post," King began. "They appear to be saying that, basically, it’s terrible what happened to you, but the bottom line is that you’re a narcissist. What do you say to that?"

Manganiello appeared a bit shocked before he replied, "Well, I think anybody who said that should read the book first and understand what the book is actually about because it’s not about that. It’s about the suffering I went through."

"Bloodlines: A Memoir" released on Oct. 13.

item.title: Abby Summers might be a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader, but her trip across the pond proves she's an Eagles fan
item.description: Cooper DeJean and Abby Summers face their biggest relationship test yet when the Eagles host the Cowboys on Monday Night Football in Philadelphia.
item.content:encoded:
We're through the first five weeks of the NFL season, and I'm here to report that Cooper DeJean and Abby Summers continue to choose love over divisional rivalry. It's a beautiful thing to witness.

Forget any forced narratives being pushed by the league. The relationship between the Philadelphia Eagles defensive back and the Dallas Cowboys cheerleader should be getting a lot more attention.

This is a romance that's defying all odds in the NFC East. These two are making it work despite being members of opposing franchises. Week 5 of the long season showed their commitment.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Abby was on the sideline and participated in the halftime show on Thursday night as the Cowboys lost at home to the backup quarterback-led Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

By Sunday, she had traded in her pom-poms and the iconic Cowboys cheerleader outfit for Eagles green as Philadelphia lost in unbelievable fashion to the Jacksonville Jaguars across the pond in London.

COWBOYS HIRE LONGTIME NFL COACH OUT OF RETIREMENT TO ADDRESS TEAM'S BRUTAL DEFENSIVE START

Now don't go around pointing fingers at Abby Summers as if she's responsible for the Eagles loss. That's not fair. They had that game in the bag until the crazy kickoff decision at the end.

That's not her fault.

As far as any of us know, mostly because she wasn't one of the WAGs who popped in the NFL's propaganda campaign, she wasn’t keeping Cooper DeJean out of the film room during training camp for social media videos.

How each of them bounces back after tough losses will tell a lot about what the season has in store for them. In a couple of weeks, we'll know even more.

That's because the Cowboys and Eagles will play each other for the first time this season, and it will be on Monday Night Football in Philadelphia. That's going to be the first real test of this relationship.

Flying out and playing WAG in London is one thing. Doing it at Lincoln Financial Field as a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader is something completely different.

If Cooper DeJean and Abby Summers can make it through that, they can make it through anything. Including a game on Thanksgiving in Dallas.

I'm not rooting for either team, but I will continue to root for the rival couple.

item.title: Rams OL Alaric Jackson expecting two-game suspension after punching Bills defender Bradley Chubb
item.description: Footage shows Alaric Jackson throwing a bare-knuckle punch at Bradley Chubb after the Rams-Bills game, and a two-game NFL suspension is looming.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL is expected to suspend Los Angeles Rams left tackle Alaric Jackson for two games after punching Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb after Monday night’s shootout and potential Super Bowl preview.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Footage of Jackson's tirade is indisputable, and the consequences are entirely self-inflicted. Monday night’s childish spectacle saw Jackson marching into the midfield, losing his cool, and throwing a bare-knuckle punch at Chubb. Jackson is expected to appeal the suspension.

The official suspension statement read, in part: "After the game, as players were shaking hands and exchanging jerseys, Jackson struck Buffalo linebacker Bradley Chubb in the face after a brief confrontation, violating Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."

Chubb, to his credit, took the higher road and kept his composure, letting Buffalo teammates pull him back, and allowed Jackson to bury himself on national television. He understood what Jackson couldn't: the cameras are running, and the bill always comes due.

RAMS OFFENSIVE LINEMAN PUNCHES BILLS LINEBACKER AFTER THRILLING GAME: 'TEMPERS GOT FLARED'

After the game, Chubb gave his reaction. "It's just emotions," he said, "They always catch the second guy. So, I let him swing. And then my teammates held me back, and I just chilled."

Chubb is a smart man; Jackson, not so much.

With Alaric Jackson, poor judgment is more of a pattern than a fluke.

Just four months ago, in June 2026, Jackson was arrested on charges of felony domestic violence in Southern California.

While prosecutors bypassed formal criminal charges in favor of a pre-filing diversion hearing, the incident remains subject to ongoing NFL review.

In 2024, the league slapped Jackson with a two-game suspension under the Personal Conduct Policy after he recorded intimate encounters on his phone without consent, an incident that later triggered a civil lawsuit.

NFL FACING A DOMESTIC VIOLENCE EPIDEMIC THIS OFFSEASON WITH ARREST OF RAMS LINEMAN THE LATEST CASE

At some point, the headaches are eclipsing the talent. Rams coach Sean McVay preaches accountability and culture, yet his starting tackle keeps showcasing eye-rolling volatility.

The Rams sit at 2-3 in a tight NFC race, desperately needing stability to protect Matthew Stafford’s blind side. Jackson will be out of action when his team needs him most.

item.title: Pentagon pushes hypersonic weapons production as startups slash costs
item.description: Dark Eagle missiles could cost over $40 million each, but startups like Castelion aim to produce hypersonic weapons for under $500,000 apiece.
item.content:encoded:
As the U.S. works to refill its missile stockpile, it is also looking to develop new weapons for its arsenal.

"We're going to need all three tiers of missiles. The cheap ones, the ones that are now the high-end like Patriot and then maybe some hypersonics," said Mark Cancian, a retired U.S. Marines colonel and senior advisor with the CSIS Defense and Security Department.

The U.S. military is taking an increasing interest in hypersonic weapons, which are maneuverable and travel five times faster than the speed of sound.

"These hypersonic systems are now seen as the novel revolutionary system and the ballistic missile is seen as the archaic one," said UC Berkeley Senior Research Scholar Cameron Tracy.

US FALLS BEHIND IN HYPERSONIC RACE AS CHINA, RUSSIA GAIN EDGE

But the weapons the military has traditionally invested in could come at a cost. Estimates from the Government Accountability Office show missiles for the Army’s long-range hypersonic weapon, the Dark Eagle, could cost more than $40 million each. As the Navy works to equip its Zumwalt Destroyers with hypersonics, the GAO puts estimates at $70 million per missile, which includes costs to develop and incorporate the necessary technologies. The GAO also notes the modernization project is two years behind schedule.

"In the long run, for example, the Army thinks that the long-ranged hypersonic weapon will become cheaper as production ramps up," said Xiaodon Liang, arms control association senior policy analyst for Nuclear Weapons Policy and Disarmament.

Tomahawk missiles cost around $2.6 million, according to the U.S. Navy. Army budget documents show Patriot missiles cost nearly $4 million. Precision Strike Missiles or PrSMs cost $1.6 million per unit. The U.S. Navy could buy almost 27 tomahawks for the price of one hypersonic missile aboard the Zumwalt Destroyers. The Army could buy around 25 PrSMs for the price of one Dark Eagle hypersonic weapon.

"The U.S. has invested in recent years in several of the programs that are starting to become into fruition," said Liang. "These are exquisite weapons. And I think that the military is acquiring them for exquisite purposes."

Hypersonic weapons travel up to 20 times faster than traditional missiles and an adversary’s reaction time is thought to be six times shorter. Hypersonic speeds are also vital for both evading enemy defense systems and executing strikes. The Atlantic Council estimates 75% fewer hypersonic weapons would be needed for a mission.

US ARMY OFFERING DEFENSE FIRMS 'CONCIERGE ACCESS' TO TEST WEAPONS AT MILITARY RANGES

Startups are hoping to bring down some of the costs to produce hypersonic weapons with more affordable missiles and increased testing capabilities.

"The weapon itself is under $500,000, which, if you know about munitions, that's incredibly cheap," Castelion co-founder and CEO Bryon Hargis said.

The Army and Navy are investing in Castelion's Blackbeard hypersonic weapon, which the company says is designed for mass production.

"It is a story about hypersonics and what they can provide in terms of a weapon, but it's really a story of American manufacturing," Hargis said. "The company is focused on providing America options to have that middle deterrence layer, and we're doing that through production."

This year, Castelion began building what it says will be the largest dedicated hypersonic weapon production factory in the U.S. Project Ranger is expected to produce thousands of Blackbeard weapons annually. Those will eventually be used to fill Castelion’s various contracts, such as integrating the weapons into the U.S. Navy's F/A-18 Super Hornet Jets, incorporating the system into the U.S. Army’s HIMARS and deploying Blackbeard on unmanned surface vessels.

"The advantage of a hypersonic system is that it goes very far, it gets there quickly and it's highly survivable because of that maneuverability. And that's important for achieving deterrence because it's hard to shoot down," Hargis said.

Hypersonic weapons remain mostly in Earth’s atmosphere. The missiles are maneuverable during flight and can strike a target quickly, in 15-30 minutes from around 1,725 miles away.

US REBUILDING WEAPONS STOCKPILE COULD DELAY ORDERS FROM ALLIES

"If you don't know what the target would be initially, unlike a ballistic missile where you can calculate where it'll land, you might misinterpret, for example, an incoming strike as a decapitation attempt. And that would be very concerning," Liang said.

Developers say the U.S. speaks with other countries about missile launches and what the intended targets are. But there are other concerns that hypersonic maneuverability could lead to inaccuracy.

"Technologies do tend to improve over time as testing and especially as experience with use builds up, but there are pretty important physical constraints on the performance of these systems," said Tracy.

Defense contractor Rocket Lab is working with the War Department to improve hypersonic missile capabilities through an increasing number of test launches.

INSIDE AMERICA'S LASER REVOLUTION AS THE MILITARY NEARS BIG BATTLEFIELD BREAKTHROUGH

"With our HASTE program, what we have enabled is low-cost, high-frequency hypersonic and missile defense testing. And when you can say that you can get that cheaper and faster, now you're looking at more of a shots on goal approach to demonstrating capability of the technology insertion cycle," Rocket Lab Vice President of Global Launch Services Brian Rogers said.

Rocket Lab’s HASTE is a suborbital test bed launch vehicle that provides flight test opportunities for the government to advance hypersonic and suborbital system technology development. The vehicle is derived from Rocket Lab’s Electron rocket, which has launched nearly 100 missions.

"Rather than saying we need to be stuck in an analysis environment, and then it's a very rigorous test campaign that costs a lot of money and involves a lot people, now you can say we're planning 12 tests this year. We don't have to bet the farm on any one of them, which allows us to take more risk and really move the needle in terms of technology development," Rogers said.

The U.S. military has never used a hypersonic weapon but has explored deploying its Dark Eagle to the Middle East.

"I would be very surprised if we used them and would be even more surprised if we used it extensively because of the small number of missiles that exist and the concerns already about the munitions stockpile," Liang said.

item.title: NYC socialist candidate says criminal record of man shot by ICE 'doesn't even matter'
item.description: Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier told Hasan Piker that Oscar Belgal's criminal record "doesn't even matter" after he was wounded in an ICE shooting.
item.content:encoded:
New York Democratic congressional candidate Darializa Avila Chevalier told Twitch streamer Hasan Piker Saturday it "doesn't even matter" that a man wounded in a shooting by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer had a criminal record.

Chevalier's comments came after Oscar Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican Republic national who the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) says is in the country illegally, was shot by an ICE officer during a targeted operation to arrest him. 

DHS said Belgal refused to comply with officers' lawful orders. 

Piker and Chevalier took issue with both New York and federal authorities highlighting Belgal's criminal history, arguing that his past crimes did not justify the use of force. 

MAMDANI DEMANDS TRUMP RELEASE ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT SHOT BY ICE AGENT AS PROTESTS ERUPT IN THE BRONX

During the encounter, Belgal pulled his vehicle forward before at least one officer fired seven rounds, striking him below his left ear, NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at a news conference near the shooting site late Thursday. Tisch also said Belgal had two prior arrests, including for robbery and the criminal sale of a controlled substance.

According to DHS, Belgal has a prior grand larceny conviction and previous arrests for assault, robbery, drug possession and weapons possession. Federal authorities also said he has ties to the notorious Trinitarios street gang.

"What is the rap sheet for this person that Jessica Tisch is alleging is this criminal, and that the ICE apprehension was valid from that perspective?" Piker asked.

"You know, I was just so angry as I was listening to it," Chevalier said. "I have gone back to her remarks to make sure that I was correct in our statement about it. But to me, it doesn’t even matter, right? It doesn’t even matter."

MAMDANI CALLS ICE A 'ROGUE' AGENCY AFTER NYC SHOOTING, CLAIMS AGENTS VIEW LAW AS 'MERELY A SUGGESTION'

Piker added that even if Belgal committed violent crimes like murder, it would not justify the ICE shooting. Chevalier also criticized Tisch for attempting to "villainize" Belgal.

"Police Commissioner Tisch came out, and I understand that it is her role to provide more information, and that is why she comes to these press conferences. But rather than condemn ICE, rather than condemn the shooting or the events that had just taken place, she started to villainize Oscar, right? Villainize him, and, by extension, villainize anyone who was in his position," Chevalier said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Chevalier's campaign for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

An NYPD spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "The Police commissioner was giving a factual update on the incident, and we always provide criminal history in incident updates if we have it. It’s also one of the first questions that every media outlet asks the NYPD."

HARRY STYLES ADDRESSES ICE SHOOTING IN NEW YORK WITH CALL FOR ‘DIGNITY AND JUSTICE’

The New York State Republican Committee criticized Chevalier's comments, calling them "further proof" that the Democratic Party has fallen.

"The facts of this case are clear: An illegal immigrant and known gang member resisted arrest and was met with lawful use of force from our brave ICE agents," NY GOP communications director David Laska told Fox News Digital. 

"The new face of the Democratic Party went on a podcast hosted by a radical who believes America deserved 9/11 to openly side with the illegal immigrant gang member — further proof that today’s Democratic Party is extremist and anti-American to its core.

"Americans will remember when we cast our ballots in November."

item.title: Bears' Montez Sweat suspended 2 games for violating NFL's performance-enhancing drug policy
item.description: Montez Sweat's two-game NFL suspension for performance-enhancing drugs leaves the Chicago Bears' defensive line thin with Dayo Odeyingbo also hurt.
item.content:encoded:
Chicago Bears defensive end Montez Sweat was suspended two games without pay for violating the NFL's performance-enhancing drug policy.

Sweat, who is in his eighth NFL season, his third full year with the Bears, will miss Chicago's Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons and Week 7 against the New England Patriots.

The 30-year-old will be reinstated by the league on Oct. 23.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The substance Sweat tested positive for was not disclosed.

Sweat’s suspension comes at a time when the Bears are already dealing with trouble on the defensive line in terms of personnel. Dayo Odeyingbo left the Bears’ blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday with a quad injury, and he never returned to the game.

As of Monday, head coach Ben Johnson didn’t provide an update on Odeyingbo.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The Bears did, however, activate Shemar Turner off the physically unable to perform list. He had been recovering from a torn ACL he suffered on Oct. 26, 2025.

But defensive coordinator Dennis Allen said it "would be unrealistic to think" anyone off the PUP list would be ready for "50, 60, 70 plays in a game." So, Turner’s addition isn’t one that can take over the workload that Sweat provides, at least in the immediate.

This season, Sweat has tallied seven tackles and two sacks across the Bears’ first five games.

item.title: Billy Crystal says he no longer trusts God after losing home of 46 years then his longtime friend Rob Reiner
item.description: Billy Crystal says he no longer trusts God after losing his Pacific Palisades home in the wildfires and the death of close friend Rob Reiner.
item.content:encoded:
Billy Crystal is opening up about how a devastating year changed his relationship with God.

During an interview with CBS Sunday Morning, the comedian, 78, opened up about how losing his longtime Pacific Palisades home in the January 2025 wildfires and the death of his close friend Rob Reiner greatly impacted his faith.

Crystal was asked whether he had been speaking with God after the painful losses. The actor referenced his previous one-man show, "700 Sundays," in which he described conversations with God, before offering a stark response.

BILLY CRYSTAL DESCRIBES PAIN OF LOSING HOME IN PALISADES FIRE AT FIREAID BENEFIT CONCERT: ‘FELL TO MY KNEES’

"No, ’cause I don’t trust Him," Crystal said.

"Too many bad things have happened," he added. "The Earth is in bad shape. This is a weird, scary time. So no, not anymore."

Crystal’s longtime home was destroyed in the Palisades fire after he and his wife, Janice, lived there for 46 years. The couple raised their children and grandchildren in the house, which Crystal described as a "magical place."

Speaking at a benefit weeks after the disaster, Crystal recalled visiting the remains of what was once his home.

ERIKA KIRK PENS ESSAY ON GRIEF AS READERS GAIN INSIGHTS INTO WRENCHING PAST YEAR

"When we were finally able to get back to our house in the Palisades, which I lived in for 46 years, like thousands of you, our house now looked like this," Crystal said, before a photo of the aftermath of the Palisades Fire appeared on the screen.

"I stepped onto the grounds and fell to my knees and I wailed. I had not cried like that since I was 15 years old, and I was told that my father had just died. I remember looking in the mirror back then with my whole life ahead of me thinking, ‘What’s my life gonna be like without him?'"

"And now folks, I'm 76-years-old, without a mirror and a lot less life to ponder thinking, ‘What is my life going to be like without our home?’" Crystal asked.

The loss became the inspiration for Crystal’s new Broadway show, "860," which is named after the street address of the home. The production recreates his home office onstage and explores his family, career, memories and grief.

NICK REINER INDICTED IN MURDERS OF PARENTS ROB REINER, MICHELE SINGER REINER AT BRENTWOOD HOME

"860" also reflects on the loss of Reiner, who was killed with his wife, Michele, in December 2025. Crystal said he and Reiner had been together at a holiday party the night before their deaths.

"We said goodbye," Crystal recalled. "And then … what?!?"

Despite the tragedies, Crystal said humor has helped him move forward.

"That’s what I do," he said when asked how he finds humor during the darkest moments. "It’s a healer."

Crystal said performing "860" has already helped him process the loss of his home and friends.

"I’ve absorbed the biggest pains that people couldn’t go through — the loss of home, dearest of friends," he said. "And I’m OK."

item.title: ‘Bonnie and Clyde’ illegal immigrant couple accused of brazen jewelry theft spree across four states
item.description: Homeland Security says the Romanian couple dubbed "Bonnie and Clyde" used hugs and fake directions to steal necklaces from elderly victims in four states.
item.content:encoded:
An illegal immigrant couple dubbed "Bonnie and Clyde" by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) allegedly turned strangers’ kindness into a payday, stealing necklaces from elderly victims in a jewelry theft spree stretching across four states.

Rudi Lacatusu, 28, and Mirabela Lacatusu, 26, Romanian nationals accused of targeting victims on Long Island, are now in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody, DHS announced Tuesday.

The pair allegedly carried out at least 14 jewelry thefts across New York, New Jersey, Connecticut and Maryland, according to DHS, which cited local reporting. 

The stolen necklaces were valued between $2,000 and $3,000 each.

DHS BOSS REVEALS OVAL OFFICE PLAN TO 'WITHHOLD FUNDING' FROM SANCTUARY CITIES AFTER AGGRESSIVE NEW YORK BUST

One alleged encounter began with a seemingly innocent request for directions.

A 73-year-old woman was standing outside her Valley Stream, New York, home Oct. 5, when a gold Mitsubishi with a man and woman inside pulled up, Nassau County police said. The female passenger asked how to get to BJ’s Wholesale Club.

After the woman helped, the passenger stepped out, asked to hug her and placed two gold-colored necklaces around her neck, according to detectives.

A short time later, the woman realized her own gold necklace, worth approximately $2,000, was gone.

Investigators linked the suspects to similar thefts in Franklin Square and East Meadow. Each faces three counts of fourth-degree grand larceny, police said.

DHS said Nassau County authorities turned the couple over to ICE after their arrests. Both entered the U.S. illegally at an unknown time and location, according to DHS.

DOJ SUES CONNECTICUT, NEW HAVEN OVER SANCTUARY POLICIES: 'OPEN DEFIANCE'

"This ‘Bonnie and Clyde’ illegal alien couple from Romania has been charged with grand larceny after allegedly carrying out more than a dozen jewelry thefts across four states," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said.

"Thanks to local partners in New York, these illegal aliens are in ICE custody and will be removed from our country."

Mullin also took aim at Democrat New York Gov. Kathy Hochul, arguing that sanctuary policies put Americans at risk.

"If it were up to sanctuary politicians like Governor Kathy Hochul, these criminals would be back on the streets to rob more Americans," he said.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S IMMIGRATION PUSH FUELS ICE'S BIGGEST ARREST MONTH IN AGENCY HISTORY

DHS used the arrests to renew its criticism of New York’s sanctuary policies, calling the state a "hotbed of illegal alien crime" under Hochul. DHS also argued those policies have had "disastrous consequences" beyond New York’s borders.

The announcement follows Operation Rotten Apple, an ICE crackdown that ran from July 27 through Aug. 29. 

DHS said officers arrested 2,197 illegal immigrants across New York during the operation, including people the department described as murderers, rapists, child predators, drug traffickers and violent assailants.

Nassau County police initially issued the suspects appearance tickets directing them to court in Hempstead Oct. 20, according to the department’s arrest announcement. DHS’ statement Tuesday did not specify when ICE took custody of them.

The case prompted police to warn residents about distraction scams targeting elderly people, including strangers offering jewelry or gifts, asking to pray together, requesting change or seeking help with a flat tire.

While a victim’s attention is elsewhere, the thieves can remove jewelry directly from their body, police warned.

Authorities urged residents to stay alert in parking lots and outside grocery stores and call 911 to report suspicious activity. 

Anyone who has been targeted in a similar theft can contact Nassau County Crime Stoppers at 1-800-244-TIPS.

item.title: Major League Baseball is experimenting with new rules this fall to fundamentally change the sport
item.description: Beyond the infield shift ban, MLB is now testing outfield positioning rules in the Arizona Fall League to combat plunging fly ball batting averages.
item.content:encoded:
Beyond the ill-informed effort to demand an unnecessary salary cap in baseball, one of the primary points of discussion around the sport have been the decline in offensive production.

Strikeouts continue to increase, while league-wide batting averages have declined. There's an endless discussion around the importance of situational hitting, of putting the ball in play, and the supposed lack of talent among modern hitters.

This "back in my day" thinking is wrong for any number of reasons, including the mountain of data we now have demonstrating it, but it ignores several key factors that have impacted the on-field product. Major League Baseball, though, realizes that the reduced run scoring environment doesn't always make for the most exciting viewing. And they're right.

DODGERS DYNASTY ON THE BRINK AFTER THE MILWAUKEE BABIP MACHINE DIALS UP ANOTHER WIN FOR BREWERS

One of their initial efforts to combat the surge in run prevention was to restrict infield shifting. For years, infielders were allowed to stand virtually anywhere, including in some extreme cases, in the middle of the outfield. Those shifts significantly reduced the likelihood of ground balls to the pull side turning into hits, as they had for most of baseball history.

The league issued some specific guidelines about extreme positioning, essentially requiring shortstops and second basemen to remain on their side of second base, among other changes. Mostly, it worked.

League-wide, batting averages on ground balls surged after baseball instituted new rules. Here's how it's looked since 2018:

While still low, the mid-.240's represents a significant increase from the shift era. Fans though, might not have noticed more ground ball hits, and the data bears that out. For example, in 2018, there were nearly 54,000 at-bats that ended with a ground ball. In 2026, there were just over 51,000, but a similar number of hits. Ground ball batting average is up, but total overall hits haven't changed.

Why would that be? More fly balls. Which is exactly what the league is hoping to address with its potential changes.

Thanks to years of data analysis, baseball front offices know that the greatest likelihood of positive outcomes comes from hitting the ball in the air. Theoretically. The best hitters in the league hit the ball hard, and hit in the air. Thanks to the advent of pitch metrics, pitch shaping, and the endless parade of 100mph relievers, hitting in general has gotten harder than ever. Front offices then, have prioritized finding players who might not make contact as frequently, but generate high-quality contact when they do. The data bears that out; outcomes on fly balls and line drives are significantly better than grounders.

In 2018, for example, the league hit .402 with a .770 slugging percentage when hitting the ball in the air, compared to .236 with a .258 slugging percentage on ground balls.

Here's the problem though, which is what MLB is hoping to address: thanks to the advent of Statcast and the limitless data now available to teams on hitter propensities, defensive positioning is now so good that teams are dramatically reducing success rates on fly balls and liners.

We'll get into the data in a minute, but here's a perfect example of this phenomenon from Monday night's NLCS game between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Milwaukee Brewers.

To set the scene, the Dodgers had a rally going against Logan Henderson, putting runners at first and second base with nobody out in the top of the third inning in a 1-1 game. Henderson threw Freddie Freeman an awful 0-1 changeup that wound up right in the perfect hitting zone for a left-handed batter. Freeman crushed it, 106.4 mph with a 22 degree launch angle, straight to the right center field gap. Balls put in play with those characteristics are hits 84% of the time, per the league's Statcast page. For the entirety of baseball history, it was a prototypical double.

Instead, right fielder Sal Frelick was positioned perfectly, and ran the ball down without even needing to dive. Instead of a bases-clearing double that scores two runs and sets up a potential big inning, it's a fly ball out.

Want to know why offense is down? That right there.

Despite their reputation as a "play the game the right way" old-school, "back in my day" team, the Brewers use analytics as much, or more, than any team in baseball. Their front office analyzes every single batted ball from Freddie Freeman against right-handed pitchers throwing exactly the type of pitches Logan Henderson throws, then tells their fielders to set up where he's most likely to hit the ball. What a surprise, they were right. And it might have helped them win game two by preventing a big inning.

Sure enough, league-wide, teams have gotten increasingly good at limiting offense on fly balls and line drives thanks to defensive positioning.

Here's the batting average and slugging percentage from across baseball since 2018 on balls in the air.

It's still significantly better to hit the ball in the air than on the ground, but as the data shows, league-wide batting averages on fly balls has dropped dramatically, a whopping 35 points from the "juiced ball" 2019 season, and roughly 20 points from 2018 or 2021.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

That's why offense is down; teams are increasingly good at positioning their fielders. Both in the left-right direction and, just as importantly, by playing deeper than ever. And MLB might be looking to stop it.

FanGraphs reported on the apparent test of new defensive positioning rules being tested in the Arizona Fall League, a typical first stop on the long road to new MLB rules.

Per their report, "sources indicated to me that the league’s motivation is to see if further limiting the locations where defenders are allowed to stand will create more base-hit action and have a positive impact on the game’s aesthetics."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

How's this working in practice?

"Dark green hash marks have been painted on the outfield grass and at points along the arc where the infield dirt meets the outfield grass," the report says. "Defenders have to stand within a certain distance of these hash marks when a pitch is thrown."

It continues, "In this alignment, infielders are forced to play 'straight up,' while the corner outfielders are closer to the foul lines, and the center fielder is more shallow compared to where we see big league outfielders normally play nowadays.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"The Hawkeye system that tracks balls and strikes, as well as the locations of balls in play and players’ on-field locations, is being used to monitor where the defenders are relative to these painted anchor points on the field. Above the stands, hanging just beneath the press box and visible from the field, are LED boards that show the players whether they are in compliance with the location restrictions."

That's fascinating. And maybe a good thing for baseball. Some purists will lament the incursion of more technology and specific rules governing where fielders are allowed to stand. But many of the changes MLB's made have been hated initially, but within a few years were mostly unnoticed or even celebrated. The pitch clock has been unambiguously good, speeding up game times while increasing the action on the field. Ending infield shifts has worked, though its effects might not have been as dramatic as hoped for.

But restricting outfield positioning could fundamentally change baseball by dramatically increasing offense success rates on the type of quality contact teams, players, and fans, have been conditioned to value over years of watching the sport. It would also increase the importance of athleticism and skill among outfielders. The lumbering left fielder whose poor defense can be papered over with excellent positioning suddenly will have to cover more ground. Faster hitters who can push the ball into the gaps will be able to take advantage of their speed and get the extra base.

Pitching is harder to hit than it's ever been. Starters and relievers throw harder, and with more

item.title: Missouri Tigers head coach Eli Drinkwitz calls fan message boards a 'cesspool' during Ahmad Hardy update
item.description: Eli Drinkwitz fired back at fan message boards over persistent Ahmad Hardy return questions, calling them a "cesspool" after Mizzou's 5-1 start.
item.content:encoded:
Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz is off to a fantastic first half of the season for 2026.

The Tigers are 5-1 and are riding high after dismantling both Florida and Texas A&M at home in back-to-back weeks.

Drinkwitz himself has to be feeling pretty good, too, considering his team has done all of this despite missing perhaps their best player in running back Ahmad Hardy.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Hardy was a unanimous All-American in 2025, and the expectations were for him to replicate that success this season, but a gunshot wound in May brought all of those ideas to a screeching halt.

The standout running back has since recovered and is miraculously working his way back to getting onto the football field.

Despite this, there is no definitive timetable for his return, and even though coach Drinkwitz has repeatedly said as much, the questions still persist at every one of his weekly pressers.

I guess this week in particular was the final straw for the man they call Drink, because the exasperated head coach offered up a final statement on the matter while taking a shot at the very place the rumors about his running back likely started.

"I really don't want to have to answer that question every week," a clearly frustrated Drinkwitz explained. "I will tell you all when there’s an update. Contrary to what’s on the cesspool of message boards."

Spicy!

Drink isn't even the first coach to fire back at that subset of his own fanbase, as Texas A&M head coach Mike Elko had some comments for the TexAgs message boards after their loss to these very same Missouri Tigers on Saturday.

Elko even invoked that same "cesspool" phrase when singling them out.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Drinkwitz is known to be a bit of a trash talker, so was this his way of getting one last jab in on A&M before moving on to planning for Ole Miss this weekend?

Maybe.

The Tigers are off to their fourth consecutive 5-1 start under Drinkwitz, and their head coach is definitely strutting his stuff on the microphone week in and week out.

Deservedly so, too.

If Mizzou pulls off the win on the road in Oxford, his postgame presser might turn into a vintage WWE promo.

It's Drink's world right now, and we are all just living in it.

item.title: Judi Dench blasts 'trigger warnings' ruining stories: 'Drives me wild'
item.description: Actress Judi Dench called trigger warnings in theater and movies "mollycoddling" in her upcoming memoir, arguing audiences should expect to be provoked.
item.content:encoded:
Dame Judi Dench decried trigger warnings in theaters and movies as "mollycoddling," telling U.K. outlet The Times Friday that it "drives [her] wild" to see them.

The 91-year-old English actress expressed the thoughts in an excerpt for Dench's upcoming memoir, "Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It?" 

As a stage and screen veteran, Dench claimed that placing trigger warnings in front of productions has gone beyond age limits or sound effects.

"I think they have gone too far," Dench said. "It's mollycoddling. If you're that sensitive, don't go to the theater.

UNIVERSITY THAT PUT OVER 200 TRIGGER WARNINGS ON SHAKESPEARE WRITINGS SAYS REQUEST CAME FROM STUDENTS

"By all means, keep the warnings about strobe lighting and gunshots, and obviously there should be age limits for children, but that's about it. Otherwise, where will it end?"

Dench also joked that trigger warnings have potentially ruined classic stories by removing surprises and watering down provocative content.

"The trigger warnings before 'Titus Andronicus' would be longer than the play. And if you overdo the warnings, doesn’t it take away from the audience’s enjoyment of the story? Do you tell them that the butler did it in an Agatha Christie play so as not to shock them? 

"Besides, in the safety of a theater or cinema, I want to be triggered, excited, stimulated, provoked and disturbed, to be taken out of my comfort zone. Isn’t that what makes theater and films so thrilling?" Dench said.

‘HOUSE OF THE DRAGON’ STAR MATT SMITH SLAMS TRIGGER WARNINGS ON TV SHOWS: ‘ISN’T BEING SHOCKED THE POINT?’

"And who knows what might trigger people? Balloons, clowns, buttons. ... I have a friend who doesn’t like bananas. She feels physically sick every time she sees one. Should supermarkets put up warning signs in the fruit and veg aisle? It drives me wild."

Fox News Digital reached out to Dench's representative for comment.

The English actress made similar comments about content advisories in a 2024 interview in which she expressed sympathy for some arguments but ultimately suggested those too sensitive should simply not go to the theater.

"I can see why they exist, and it is preparing people, I suppose. But if you’re that sensitive, don’t go to the theater because you could be very shocked," Dench said.

BILL MAHER RAILS AGAINST TRIGGER WARNINGS IN COLLEGES, ENTERTAINMENT: 'HOW WEAK MY COUNTRY HAS BECOME'

In a comment to Fox News Digital, film critic and "Hollywood in Toto" podcast host Christian Toto called it a "sad state of affairs" that Dench's comments would be considered surprising but celebrated them regardless.

"Dench's statement on trigger warnings is obvious, but it still needs to be said today. It's especially helpful coming from an artist. Almost anything in art can be triggering, all depending on the audience. If your beloved dog died last week, any story with a sick pup can be 'triggering.' Art is meant to challenge us, to question our beliefs and offer new perspectives on older ideas. All of the above might be triggering today," Toto said.

"So deal with it, or don't consume art. This kind of wisdom is rare in Hollywood. Kudos for Dench for lighting the way to sanity."

item.title: Woman accused of deadly revenge crash faces jury as boyfriend’s hospital account stays out of trial
item.description: Leigha Mumby's trial opened with prosecutors alleging she turned sharply into woods at nearly 100 mph after a fight over another girl's texts.
item.content:encoded:
A Florida woman accused of deliberately crashing an SUV with her boyfriend inside was furious over another girl’s text messages before making a sharp turn into the woods at nearly 100 mph, prosecutors told jurors Tuesday.

But Leigha Mumby’s defense attorney offered a different explanation as her trial opened, suggesting something happened inside the vehicle that she neither anticipated nor controlled.

Mumby, 25, has pleaded not guilty to vehicular homicide and reckless driving causing serious bodily injury in the death of Daniel Waterman, 22, who survived the crash, but died eight months later.

Assistant State Attorney Melissa Clark told jurors the couple had left a Super Bowl party before the Feb. 9, 2025, wreck on Interstate 95 in Flagler County, according to proceedings livestreamed by Court TV.

OHIO SUPREME COURT DENIES MACKENZIE SHIRILLA'S LATEST APPEAL BID IN DOUBLE MURDER CASE

Clark said the SUV traveled at speeds exceeding 100 mph before the crash. Vehicle data showed it was moving at 94 mph in the final seconds before an "abrupt, left-hand turn at 45 degrees" sent it off the highway and into the woods.

The prosecutor described the turn as "a dangerous and reckless maneuver."

Waterman suffered a broken neck that left him paralyzed from the neck down, Clark said. He fell into a coma and, after awakening, could not breathe on his own.

His death on Oct. 8, 2025, was "directly related and caused by this crash," Clark told the jury, who will not hear Waterman's own account of the crash that he told detectives before he died. 

He told investigators from his hospital bed that Mumby deliberately swerved off the road following an argument over another woman's text message. A judge ruled those statements inadmissible, leaving prosecutors unable to present his version of events at trial.

Defense attorney Reid Hart called the case a "pure and utter tragedy" and urged jurors to consider whether the SUV’s sudden change in direction resulted from something outside Mumby’s control.

"The crux of this trial effectively comes down to one steering wheel input, and ultimately one question," Hart said, according to Court TV’s livestream.

Hart questioned whether Mumby chose to drive off the road or whether something happened inside the vehicle that "she did not expect, she did not anticipate, and she did not control."

He argued that once the vehicle began careening toward the woods, she could not stop it despite trying to avoid the crash.

MACKENZIE SHIRILLA'S TEXTS SURFACE AS 'HELL ON WHEELS' DRIVER'S APPEAL COLLIDES WITH NETFLIX'S 'THE CRASH'

Jurors also heard Tuesday from Sarah Stappenbeck, Waterman’s cousin and Mumby’s best friend, who hosted the Super Bowl gathering.

Stappenbeck testified that Mumby announced earlier that day that she had learned she was pregnant. But the news came alongside concerns about Waterman’s contact with other women.

Mumby "expressed concerns of Daniel talking to other girls and said that she wasn’t going to let Daniel cheat on her," Stappenbeck testified.

The couple left before the game ended. Within about 20 minutes, Stappenbeck said, Mumby called her, yelling that Waterman was texting another girl and that she planned to bring him back to the house.

"She’s yelling at me," Stappenbeck recalled.

WATCH: MACKENZIE SHIRILLA’S FATHER CALLS HER ‘A DUMB 18-YEAR-OLD’ WHILE BERATING POLICE IN BODYCAM VIDEO

Stappenbeck said she did not hear Waterman speaking in the background. She tried to calm Mumby and urged the couple to get home safely and address their disagreement the following day.

"She just said that ‘You’re taking his side,’ and hung up with me," Stappenbeck testified.

About 20 minutes later, Mumby called again, still angry, and repeated that she was bringing Waterman back, Stappenbeck said.

They never arrived. Instead, Stappenbeck testified, Mumby’s roommate called and told her to go to the hospital because there had been a crash.

The trial is unfolding without Waterman’s account to investigators of what happened inside the SUV.

Before his death, Waterman told detectives Mumby deliberately caused the wreck after an argument over a text from another woman, according to charging documents previously reported by Court TV.

He said the last thing he remembered was Mumby telling him, "I don’t care what happens, you’ll get what you deserve," before swerving off the road.

Judge Dawn Nichols ruled those statements could not be introduced at trial. Prosecutors said they wanted jurors to hear Waterman’s account, but acknowledged the rules of evidence prevented them from using it at trial, Court TV previously reported.

"The court is bound by the law and the court is bound by the rules of evidence," Nichols said when explaining the ruling.

The first day of Mumby’s trial also brought an emotional moment for Waterman’s family. His mother, Heather Waterman, was seen wiping away tears as a photo of her son was shown in court.

Court adjourned for the day following Tuesday’s proceedings.

Mumby was initially arrested in July 2025 on charges of reckless driving causing serious bodily injury and aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.

FAMILY OF FATHER-TO-BE WHOSE GIRLFRIEND ALLEGEDLY CRASHED CAR ON PURPOSE SPEAKS OUT THROUGH LAWYER

After Waterman died, prosecutors upgraded her charges to include vehicular homicide. She was booked into the Flagler County Jail and released after posting a $150,000 bond.

Waterman’s mother previously told Syracuse.com that he spent time in a coma before recovering enough to tell investigators what happened.

Waterman’s aunt, Tiffany Waterman, expressed anguish over the exclusion of her nephew’s statements in a Facebook post Monday as jury selection began.

She remembered his efforts to comfort a loved one watching a movie beside him in his hospital bed, smiling at her while trying to conceal his pain.

"That’s who Daniel was. Protective, loving, and sweet," she wrote. "He had the biggest heart, even in those last moments of life."

The family previously told Fox News Digital through attorney John Hager that they supported the charges filed following Waterman’s death.

"There are no real winners in this situation. It’s a terrible, horrible situation," Hager said in November 2025, adding that the family believed the charges were "right and just."

Mumby gave birth to a baby girl three days after Waterman died, according to WSYR.

"Daniel was an excited, soon-to-be father of a baby girl," his obituary said. "He wanted nothing more than to come home to her and to the family who loved him so dearly."

The trial comes amid renewed attention to another deadly crash involving a young woman convicted of intentionally driving into a building with her boyfriend inside.

Mackenzie Shirilla is serving two concurrent sentences of 15 years to life for killing her boyfriend, Dominic Russo, 20, and their friend, Davion Flanagan, 19, in a 2022 crash in Strongsville, Ohio, Fox News Digital previously reported.

Shirilla’s case became the subject of Netflix’s "The Crash." 

She was convicted in 2023 after prosecutors argued she deliberately drove into a brick building at nearly 100 mph to end her relationship with Russo.

The Ohio Supreme Court recently rejected her request to reconsider its decision, declining to hear her latest appeal. Shirilla has maintained the crash was not intentional.

Fox News Digital's Michael Sinkewicz, Greg Norman, and Stephen Sorace contributed to this report.

item.title: Hochul's office mocks Katie Zacharia with Aaron Rodgers injury post despite governor's press secretary scandal
item.description: New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul's press office appeared to mock Katie Zacharia's White House debut by posting Aaron Rodgers' Jets injury photo.
item.content:encoded:
New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul’s press office appeared to mock new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia’s debut Tuesday by posting a photo of Aaron Rodgers’ entrance before the Jets game in which he suffered a season-ending injury. Hochul's own previous press secretary had to resign after sexual harassment allegations last year.

The governor’s press account shared the image while quoting a White House post announcing, "Your new White House Press Sec, @KatieZacharia, makes her debut at the podium."

The photograph shows Rodgers carrying an American flag before his first regular-season appearance for the Jets on Sept. 11, 2023, the 22nd anniversary of the terrorist attacks. His highly anticipated debut ended after just four offensive snaps when he tore his left Achilles tendon against the Buffalo Bills. He missed the remainder of the season.

TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY FACES FIRST MAJOR TEST AS WHITE HOUSE BRIEFING ROOM ENTERS NEW ERA

The juxtaposition appeared to draw a comparison between Zacharia’s introduction and Rodgers’ abruptly curtailed debut, although Hochul’s office included no written explanation with the image.

OutKick contacted the governor’s office asking what analogy it intended and whether it was comparing Zacharia’s first briefing to Rodgers’ 2023 injury.

Hochul’s own press operation previously faced a sexual harassment scandal. Her then-press secretary, Avi Small, resigned on July 4, 2025, after being placed on leave pending an investigation into a sexual harassment complaint, her office confirmed.

Small was accused of inappropriately touching a fellow staffer at an Albany bar following a June 16 staff event. The governor’s office said the investigation had "substantively concluded," but declined to disclose its findings, the New York Post reported.

"Governor Hochul has zero tolerance for misconduct by any New York State employee," her communications director, Anthony Hogrebe, said at the time, adding that Small was placed on leave as soon as the complaint reached the governor’s office.

Hochul subsequently defended her administration’s response, telling reporters, "the culture was changed, the system worked."

Many users on social media criticized Hochul's office for the Tuesday post with the previous scandal within her own press operation.

Zacharia succeeded Karoline Leavitt after President Donald Trump named her to the position Friday. Her first briefing lasted approximately 14 minutes, ending with her directing reporters to question Trump before his departure for Alaska. Trump subsequently praised her performance.

TRUMP SAYS KAROLINE LEAVITT WILL LEAVE WHITE HOUSE PRESS SECRETARY ROLE, BECOME OUTSIDE ADVISOR

"I thought she did excellent. She did very good," Trump told reporters.

The White House also praised Zacharia’s inaugural briefing in an official release highlighting her commitment to promoting Trump’s agenda and retaining the administration’s new-media seat.

Hochul’s press account has cultivated a confrontational social media presence. In a March interview with City & State, her rapid-response director described the account as a vehicle for pushing back against the Trump administration’s attacks.

item.title: Brian Flores' lawyer says memo to Raiders before team's coaching search portrayed client as 'angry Black man'
item.description: A newly unsealed Korn Ferry memo reveals harsh criticisms of Brian Flores that his lawyers say prove NFL retaliation over his discrimination lawsuit.
item.content:encoded:
The lawyers for Brian Flores say a recruiting memo used by the Las Vegas Raiders while considering the Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator for their head-coaching job is evidence that teams are retaliating against him for filing a racial discrimination lawsuit and that discriminatory hiring practices remain in place across the NFL.

The document that the NFL and search firm Korn Ferry hoped would remain sealed became public Tuesday after the magistrate judge overseeing the discovery process in Flores's class-action lawsuit previously rejected Korn Ferry's arguments to keep the document confidential.

The Korn Ferry document, as first reported by Front Office Sports, presents two columns under the heading, "Brian Flores -- Strengths and Weaknesses"

SUPREME COURT HANDS NFL A LOSS IN BRIAN FLORES DISCRIMINATION LAWSUIT

Among the Flores weaknesses, per Korn Ferry:

Flores attorney Michael Willemin told FOS some of these descriptions conjure the image of an "angry Black man." 

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Even one of the six positive points that Korn Ferry credits to Flores can be questionable in a discrimination suit because it paints Flores as someone who learned to speak and present himself positively because he got to meet rich White people despite being reared in a tough predominantly Black and Hispanic neighborhood.

The law firms representing Flores, Wigdor LLP and Elefterakis, Elefterakis & Panek, issued a statement on Tuesday about the Korn Ferry memo:

"The recently unsealed documents demonstrate two unfortunate, but unsurprising, realities," the statement reads. "First, that Mr. Flores’ decision to hold the league and its teams accountable for systemic race discrimination has been met with unlawful retaliation.

"Second, discrimination continues to play a significant role in the hiring process for NFL Head Coaches, as evidenced by the fact that the candidate profile prepared for the Raiders leans heavily on racial stereotypes. We and Mr. Flores are committed to eradicating the institutional racism and retaliation that permeates the league, its teams and their partners."

The memo in question was prepared by Korn Ferry for the Las Vegas Raiders before the team's most recent coaching search that ultimately resulted in Klint Kubiak being hired.

Flores was not interviewed by the Raiders.

Flores, who is Black, sued the NFL and its 32 teams in February 2022, specifically naming the Miami Dolphins, Denver Broncos and New York Giants. He alleged that the league’s hiring practices were "rife with racism" toward Black coaches. He was later joined in the lawsuit by fellow Black coaches Steve Wilks and Ray Horton.

Flores, who coached the Dolphins from February 2019 to January 2022, alleges in his suit that the Dolphins defamed him.

item.title: Dem candidate's bizarre anti-MAGA tirade ends with 'We have guns too'
item.description: Jaime West, a Democrat running for Fayette County Council in Indiana, drew ridicule after appearing to slur through attacks on Republicans at a forum.
item.content:encoded:
A Democrat running for county council in eastern Indiana was ridiculed Tuesday after critics claimed she appeared "s--- faced" and slurred her way through attacks on Republicans during a televised candidate forum.

During the forum, Fayette County Council candidate Jaime West said she would "fire all Republicans" if elected, railed against "MAGAs" she called "racist" and unintelligent and alleged that a sheriff’s nephew had threatened to kill her. Asked for a final message to voters, West responded: "We have guns too."

"This is not a skit," said LibsOfTikTok, a popular conservative punditry account run by commentator Chaya Raichik.

"Jaime West, a Democrat running for Fayette County Council in Indiana, gave an embarrassing interview where she appears to mumble and rant the entire time. Is she intoxicated?" Raichik asked on X.

LAWMAKER’S STUNNED FACE AND OTHER VIRAL MOMENTS CAP ROUGH WEEK FOR POLITICAL CLASS

Former litigator Viva Frei tweeted that the video initially appeared to be a "skit [or] high school video project."

"I had to make sure she did not have a neurological disorder that could account for the slurred speech and insane rambling. She doesn’t. And even if she did have a diagnosed neurological disorder, ‘we have guns too’ after talking about firing all Republicans would ordinarily be disqualifying," Frei said.

When asked one decision she would make if elected that constituents would find unpopular, West told the moderator, "Fire all Republicans."

"I wouldn’t let them — I don’t even talk to them. I don’t like them. They voted against — their own state representative voted against her own party," West continued while also pledging not to raise taxes.

DEM SENATE HOPEFULS UNDER SCRUTINY FOR ‘CHOKE THEM OUT’ RHETORIC AFTER TRUMP ATTACK SCARE

"They call you names. The sheriff’s nephew threatened to blow my head off. But, you know, what are you going to do?"

The moderator paused before asking West for a final message to voters.

West could not immediately be reached for comment. While it was not immediately clear which Indiana sheriff West was referring to, Zac Jones, who leads the Fayette County Sheriff's Office where she is running, was stunned by the remark.

"I don’t know Jaime West, and she obviously doesn’t know me. I have five nieces and zero nephews. I’m not sure what she is talking about, and I’m certain she has no idea what she is talking about either," Jones told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Tim Walz warns Democrats will face reckoning if they win power and fail to deliver change
item.description: Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz warns Democrats will face serious backlash if they win back power but fail to deliver on housing and college education.
item.content:encoded:
Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz issued a warning to his party in an interview Thursday, arguing there would be backlash if Democrats win elections in November and beyond but fail to make significant structural changes.

During an interview with "The Lever" founder David Sirota, Walz was asked if the Democratic Party had an issue offering up big promises but ultimately failing to deliver.

"Yes, a hundred percent. It’s a hundred percent," Walz said. "I always use the line, as I said, we win these elections not to bank the political capital to win the next one but to improve lives. We’re too slow about it. And some of that is structural,"

WATCH: DEMOCRATS ADMIT WHEN THEY'D ELIMINATE THE FILIBUSTER AS SAVE ACT FIGHT HEATS UP

He pointed to former Sen. Joe Manchin's position that the filibuster must remain in place in the Senate.

"Look, I’m friends with Joe Manchin, but the desire to hold onto the filibuster at all costs as an institution when it had real impacts on people’s lives of real important things, and by not doing that, it played right into the hands of the Republicans. I think we’re not responsive, and then we fall into that 'But we voted for you, and you didn’t get anything done,'" Walz said.

Manchin has been consistent in his support for the filibuster. In 2022, he and then-Sen. Kyrsten Sinema voted against changing the Senate's 60-vote threshold for advancing most legislation, opposing other Democrats who sought to change the rules to pass voting legislation.

WALZ APPROVAL RATING CRATERS TO LOWEST LEVEL EVER AND TRAILS TRUMP AMID MASSIVE FRAUD SCANDAL: 'TIRED OF IT'

Walz, the 2024 Democratic vice presidential nominee, warned of a "real danger." 

"Here’s where I think the real danger is. If there is not significant structural change — whether it’s inequities, you know, income inequities or opportunities — the backlash, because, I said this: I got into politics because I said we’ll never find a worse president than George Bush. And I think now, if you think that this is the pinnacle of how bad things can get, I would caution you to rethink that.

"And especially if Democrats do all of this, the public turns out, they vote for us and kids still can’t afford a college education, can’t afford housing. That’s going to be a problem."

He then predicted that Democrats would regain control of the House, Senate and eventually the presidency in 2028.

MN LAWMAKERS UNLOAD ON WALZ'S 'LEGACY' AFTER HE TOUTS FRAUD RECORD IN FINAL ANNUAL ADDRESS: 'RIDICULOUS'

Lindsey Drath, CEO of the Forward Party, told Fox News Digital, "We shouldn't advocate for abolishing the filibuster to drive home party-line votes with no effort to advance cross-partisan consensus law making. What hampers Congress' ability to deliver material solutions to the American people is a two-party system that penalizes working across the aisle.

"This circular dynamic, whereby Democrats or Republicans enter into a narrow majority, only to focus on maintaining power, accumulates a kind of figurative debt against the challenges facing the American people," she said. "This dynamic pushes our elected officials away from working on real solutions for actual problems and toward whatever hyper polarized means by which they can to hold on to power.

"This is why a fulcrum strategy is key," Drath continued. "The Senate today passes almost nothing on a bipartisan basis, not because the problems aren't solvable, but because neither party has any incentive to negotiate. Every compromise is a political cost. If someone crosses the aisle, they are attacked by their party. It is framed as every deal made is a loss to play at home. The incentive is to obstruct, posture and wait for the next election. 

"The fulcrum strategy is that you don't need a majority to change the Senate," she added. "You need only a handful. It uses a small bloc of independents to balance power in Congress and take away full majority from either side. With an expected closely divided Congress this cycle, this is very relevant and real. It would mean both parties would have to negotiate with those few in the middle before anything passes. The party that wants their vote has to offer something real, something that actually serves the people."

Walz announced in January that he would not seek elected office again after previously announcing he wouldn't run for a third term as governor.

He reflected on his tenure as governor in a September interview, including his handling of widespread fraud involving Minnesota social services programs.

"Fraud — should have stopped it sooner," Walz told The Minnesota Star Tribune. "We didn’t stop them. I accept that. I think there does need to be accountability with that. And part of it is that, yep, that’s with me, I’ll step aside."

The governor said the state "immediately" took action to address the fraud and then suggested that the true cost of the fraud, estimated at $9 billion by federal prosecutors, has been overstated. Walz also compared the fraud losses to the cost of President Donald Trump’s White House ballroom, which he suggested was more expensive.

"I should have been down on those agencies a little more, but I will tell you this, in the scheme of things, all the fraud that's been prosecuted, by the way, and all the fraud that's probably out there is less than the ballroom at the White House," Walz said. 

"So, it puts it into perspective. It doesn't make it right. Doesn't make it right."
